summary.title: Building a CLI command with Go: cowsay
summary.one_liner: You learn how to port the cowsay CLI to Go by reading piped stdin, wrapping text in an ASCII speech balloon, and selecting a figure (cow or stegosaurus) with a -f flag.
takeaways: Detect whether stdin is a pipe using os.Stdin.Stat and ModeCharDevice, and print usage otherwise.
Read piped input line by line and normalize line widths using rune counts so the balloon aligns.
Build a speech balloon around the text with buildBalloon, handling single-line and multi-line cases.
Use the standard flag package (flag.StringVar) to let users pick a figure such as cow or stegosaurus with -f.
Compile and install the tool with go build and go install so it runs system-wide.
summary.summary: The article walks through building a cowsay clone in Go, starting from a module named gocowsay so the binary gets that name. It begins with a simple program that reads piped stdin, then adds balloon formatting using helper functions for tab conversion, max width calculation, and padding lines by rune count. The final step introduces a printFigure function with cow and stegosaurus ASCII art, selected through a -f flag parsed with the flag package. The author notes the code was checked with Go 1.27 and ends by installing the binary with go build and go install.
